title: VPC post-deploy readiness validator and model-stress wave runner
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic post-deploy validator that runs automatically after a Private (VPC) deployment completes and verifies API readiness, model load behavior under short stress waves, and a set of intent-based smoke tests. The validator must be safe for production (non-destructive), provide clear SLO pass/fail signals, and emit structured artifacts for later analysis and alerting.

Scope:
- Terraform/CI trigger hooks: run after terraform apply finishes on private clusters (via GH Actions or pipeline job).
- API readiness probe: authenticated/unauthenticated handshake, schema validation, latency percentiles.
- Model load wave runner: sequential short-burst load (10s waves) across representative model flavors (small, medium, quantized) to verify KV cache behavior, memory stability, and eviction patterns.
- Intent-based smoke set: ~12 user-visible prompts (chat + streaming + tool-call) that exercise common code paths and structured output.
- Observability: upload logs, token-level p95 latency, OOM traces, and a summarized verdict JSON to S3/metrics back-end.
- Fail open vs fail closed: On failure, mark rollout failed and emit remediation suggestions; do not automatically revert without manual approval.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for this ticket to close):
1) The validator can be invoked as a single CI job and completes end-to-end within 12 minutes on a green Private stack.
2) Pass/fail threshold configuration is parameterized (latency p95, error rate, model load success ratio). Defaults: latency p95 < 250ms for small model, < 450ms for medium model; error rate < 1% across smoke set.
3) Generates a structured report (flat JSON) containing: invoked models, wave schedule, per-probe latencies, pass/fail per-check, captured stderr/stdout from model processes (sanitized), and S3 link to full traces.
4) Integrates with existing rollout orchestration: posts status to rollout API and creates a Linear ticket on hard failure.
5) Minimal false-positive rate in smoke runs: instrument a 2-week shadow run on staging with historical baselines and show < 5% spurious failures.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Use short waves rather than long soak tests to reduce cost and to validate startup + steady-state extremes (cold KVC, warm KV usage).
- Avoid aggressive concurrency saturations that could trigger infra autoscaler oscillation; cap parallelism per model to 6 concurrent requests.
- For safety, all test inputs are sanitized to exclude customer data; use canned prompts and internal corpora.
- Keep the validator idempotent and able to re-run in case of transient infra problems.

Runbook (high-level):
1) CI triggers job 'vpc-postdeploy-validator' after terraform job completes.
2) Terraform outputs (API endpoints, credentials, model variant matrix) passed as job inputs.
3) Validator runs API readiness probes: health endpoint check, auth token exchange, openapi schema roundtrip test.
4) Launch model-stress wave runner: for each model in matrix, run 3 waves of 10s each at increasing concurrency (1, 3, 6). Capture per-token latencies and memory metrics.
5) Execute intent-based smoke set: expect defined structured outputs and function/ tool-calls to succeed.
6) Aggregate metrics and compute pass/fail by thresholds. Upload verdict.json and link to traces/metrics dashboard.
7) If failed, annotate rollout with failure reason and create actionable notes for SRE/owner.

Implementation notes:
- Implement validator in Go as a small CLI that can be compiled into the CI image; use the existing SDK for authenticated requests.
- Use the runtime's admin endpoints for model load verification rather than driving raw GPU probing to avoid privileged access.
- Leverage Prometheus exporter endpoints and token-level tracing to capture memory and latency signals.
- Provide a dry-run flag for manual verification without creating Linear tickets or posting to rollout API.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Postdeploy+Validator (design doc + test corpus)
- GH actions workflow draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/2462
- Prototype PR (validator CLI): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5523
- Dashboard example: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/vpc-validator-run

QA plan: run on staging for 10 full runs across 5 clusters with different instance types and validate the false-positive statistics and resource overhead. Collect logs and iterate on thresholds.

Notes for follow-up: add an optional model prewarm phase that pins KV caches for customer-critical models and extend the smoke-set with tenant-specific prompts behind opt-in.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Patel: Initial ticket created; sketched design and high-level runbook. Assigned to Ethan for implementation. Leaving prototype CLI approach as preferred to simplify CI image requirements.

2026-03-04 - Ethan Zhao: Spiked a small Go CLI. Successfully executed API readiness probes against staging cluster s-vpc-10. Found disparity in health endpoint response schema between runtime v1.18 and v1.17; added compatibility shim to the CLI.

2026-03-06 - SRE Review (A. Romero): Reviewed wave schedule. Recommended capping concurrency for medium models to 4 to avoid autoscaler thrash; updated wave runner config accordingly. Added to acceptance tests.

2026-03-09 - Testing: Ran first combined validator on staging. 1 of 5 clusters failed a KV eviction check for quantized model; attaching logs to GH PR. Root cause: memory pinning disabled in runtime image (hotfix candidate).

2026-03-11 - Ethan Zhao: Hotfix PR opened to enable memory pinning for quantized builds: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5589. Retest scheduled after merge. Added dry-run mode to CLI and upload of verdict.json to S3 in human-readable and minimized forms.

2026-03-14 - Maya Patel: Security review requested due to validator uploading sanitized stderr/stdout to S3. Security provided checklist; validator must redact any potential config secrets. Marked security_review_required = true.
2026-03-14 - QA: Scheduled shadow runs for 2 weeks starting 2026-03-16 across 3 staging clusters. If shadow pass rate < 95% we will adjust default thresholds and escalate to runtime team.
notes: Keep false positives low; prefer conservative defaults. The validator should not perform destructive actions or trigger automatic rollbacks. Ensure strong logging and a single structured verdict blob for downstream automation.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for CLI behavior and threshold logic. 2) Integration tests in CI against a minimal private stack. 3) 2-week shadow run in staging to measure false-positive rate. 4) Runbook dry-runs with dry-run flag and then gated full runs on canary clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Validator completes within 12 minutes on green private stack
Configurable pass/fail thresholds and sane defaults as documented
Structured verdict.json uploaded and linked to rollout API
Integrated with rollout orchestrator to create a Linear ticket on hard failure
<5% spurious failure rate in 2-week shadow run
